lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: You're listening to Lower Hollow Community Radio. Lost pets, bake sales, and the hole.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: This is Lower Hollow Community Radio. If you hear your name called from the hole, please don't answer. It's not rude. It's policy.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Good morning, Lower Hollow. The kettle's on, the noticeboard's full, and the hole is where we left it.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Lower Hollow Community Radio, eighty nine point seven. Population, today: fluctuating. Welcome, whoever's new.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Lower Hollow Community Radio, overnight. Maureen here. Somebody has to keep an eye on things.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: People ask me, Maureen, what's in the hole? And I say, it's not my place. I'm a volunteer. I do the notices, the pets and the birthdays. Councillor Dibbs does the hole.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: That's how we've always done it, and it's worked very well. Apart from Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Something came up out of the hole this afternoon, outside the post office. Large. Pale. Quite slow. Everybody did the sensible thing, which was to say nothing and carry on queueing.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: It went back down at about four. The post office would like to remind customers that it closes at half past five regardless.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Hello to the night operator on that ship that drifts over the Hollow at about this time. We can see your little light from the rim.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Mind the hole, dear. It's bigger from above. Everything is.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: An update on Biscuit, Mister Ainsley's spaniel. Biscuit is at the hole. Biscuit is always at the hole. He isn't lost. Please stop bringing him back. He's busy.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: He's been watching the same spot since the summer, wagging very slightly. Whatever's down there, Biscuit thinks it's a good boy.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Mrs Crabtree on Rim Lane reports a shadow sitting on her garden wall each evening. No person attached. Wears a little hat. Very polite. Leaves before the street lamps come on.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: She's given it a cushion. Hollis, dear, if he's yours, he's fine. He likes the view.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: And now, the community noticeboard. If it's pinned up at the post office, you'll hear it here first.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Time for the notices. Pen and paper ready, please. Not the blue pen. You know who you are.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: The Hollow Bakers' Circle bake sale is this Saturday, on the green. Lemon drizzle, flapjacks, and Edna's fruit cake, which has never once been finished.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: A reminder. Please don't feed anything to the hole. Last year it took a whole Victoria sponge, and we had a very awkward week.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Lost. A grey tabby called Duchess, missing from Rim Lane since Monday. Answers to Duchess, or to the sound of a tin opening.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: If you see her, please don't chase her towards the edge. Just open a tin and wait. She'll come. They always come for a tin.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Found. One black umbrella, which came up out of the hole on Tuesday morning, perfectly dry, and opened itself on the green.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: It's at the post office. If it's yours, please collect it. Please don't explain.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: The Lower Hollow choir meets on Thursdays at seven, in the church hall. New voices very welcome, especially tenors.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: If you hear an extra voice during the low hymns, coming from somewhere below, carry on. Don't harmonise with it. It only encourages it.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Jumble sale at the Scout hut on Sunday. Books, toys, bric-a-brac, and a quantity of single shoes, all left feet, which came up out of the hole over the summer.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: If you've lost a left shoe, it may well be here. If you've lost a right shoe, we can't help you, and frankly, we're worried.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Happy birthday to Mrs Ivy Cole of Rim Cottages, who is ninety two today. Ivy has lived on the rim all her life.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: She says the secret to a long life is a boiled egg every morning, and never looking down for more than a minute. Happy birthday, Ivy. Have an egg.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Found on the green. A letter, addressed to the Hole Committee, in very neat handwriting, with no stamp. It came up on the wind.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Councillor Dibbs has it. He's read it. He's gone very quiet. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: That's the noticeboard. If you've a notice of your own, pop it through my door. My door, please. Not the hole.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: And that's all the notices for now. Be good to each other, and stay on the town side of the rim.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: And now the council update, with the chair of the Hole Committee, Councillor Dibbs.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: Thank you, Maureen.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: Good evening. Councillor Dibbs, chair of the Hole Committee, with the council update.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: The committee met on Thursday. Item one. The hole. The committee noted the hole.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: Item two. The fence around the hole. The committee noted that the fence is now also, somewhat, in the hole. A new fence has been ordered. It will be placed slightly further back, as is customary.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: Several residents have asked the committee what the hole is. The committee thanks residents for their interest. The committee has been asked this question every week for thirty years.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: And the committee is pleased to say that it has, after careful consideration, once again decided to move on to item three.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: A reminder of the by-law concerning objects thrown into the hole. Anything thrown into the hole becomes, in law, a gift.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: The hole is not obliged to send a thank-you note. It has, on four occasions, sent one anyway. These are on file.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: The proposal from the Lower Hollow Radio Club, to lower a microphone into the hole, has been rejected. The committee wishes to reassure the radio club that this is not personal.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: It is simply that the last time a microphone was lowered, in nineteen eighty one, it was returned. With a recording on it. Which the committee has listened to, and will not be discussing.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: The annual hole inspection. The inspector lowered himself to the usual depth, took the usual readings, and came back up with the usual expression.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: He has submitted his report. The report reads, in full: yes. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: That concludes the council update.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: The hole remains. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: The next meeting is on Thursday, in the church hall. Please bring a chair. Not one of the old ones. They lean.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Lower Hollow Community Radio, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: Ron, Rim Lane
lines.text: Hello, Maureen. It's Ron, from Rim Lane.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Hello, Ron. How's the knee?

lines.speaker: Ron, Rim Lane
lines.text: Better, thanks. Maureen, I want to put fairy lights up round the hole for the winter. All the way round.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: That's a lot of lights, Ron.

lines.speaker: Ron, Rim Lane
lines.text: I've got a lot of lights. Is it allowed?

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: I'll ask. Councillor?

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: The committee has no objection to lights. The committee asks only that you don't run the cable over the edge.

lines.speaker: Ron, Rim Lane
lines.text: Why not?

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: Because the last time, something plugged itself in.

lines.speaker: Ron, Rim Lane
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Lovely, Ron. Send us a picture.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Good morning, and welcome to Morning Notices. I'm Maureen. The overnight report: the hole is still there. It was quiet. Mostly.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: The overnight hole report. At two this morning, a warm breeze came up out of the hole, smelling of toast. At three, the toast smell stopped.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: At four, a single yellow balloon came up, and drifted east. That's the report. Have a lovely day.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: This morning's birthdays. Happy birthday to young Ellie Marsh, who is seven.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: And happy birthday to the hole, which, according to the parish records, is either four hundred years old, or always.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: Good evening. This is the Committee Hour, on Lower Hollow Community Radio. The hole remains. Item one.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: Correspondence. The committee has received a letter from the hole. It was very well written. The committee has replied, thanking it for its letter, and noting its contents.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: What did it say, Councillor?

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: It has been noted, Maureen.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: Any other business. Mister Ainsley asks whether he may take his dog home from the rim.

lines.speaker: Councillor Dibbs
lines.text: The committee has considered the question, and notes that this is a matter for the dog.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: This is Rim Watch. Maureen here, with a flask, a blanket and the binoculars. You go to sleep, dear. I'll keep an eye on it.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Quarter past three. The lamps are on over on the far rim, and nobody lives over there, as far as anyone knows. I've waved.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Somebody has waved back. That's neighbourly. I'll take it.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Very quiet tonight. Biscuit's asleep at the edge, one ear up. The flask's half done. Every so often there's a sound from the hole like somebody turning over in bed.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: I always say, goodnight, then. It seems only polite.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: A Halloween reminder for trick-or-treaters. Please stay on the town side of the rim.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Last year, something came up out of the hole wearing a sheet with two eye holes cut in it, and won the costume contest. Nobody knows who it was. It comes back every year to collect the prize.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: We've let it keep the rosette.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: The pumpkin carving results. Third place, Ellie Marsh, for a lovely cat. Second, the Ainsleys, for a very good owl.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: And first place, a pumpkin nobody entered, which came up out of the hole on Thursday, carved from the inside. It's very good. It's smiling. It's been smiling at the post office all week.
